Question B-006-005-010.

Why the correct answer is right: An antenna analyzer sweeps or checks frequencies and reports the antenna-system impedance and SWR, so it shows where the system is matched or mismatched across a frequency range.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Radiation pattern of the antenna": Radiation pattern requires measuring field strength around the antenna or modelling the antenna geometry; a one-port analyzer at the feed line cannot map the pattern.
- sourceIndex 2: "Gain of the antenna": Antenna gain requires comparison with a reference antenna or calibrated field measurements; an analyzer reading at the feed point does not directly give gain.
- sourceIndex 3: "Front-to-back ratio of the antenna": Front-to-back ratio is found by comparing radiation in opposite directions, so it is a pattern measurement rather than an impedance-analyzer result.
